titulo.en: Passing on what someone says

texto.en: To pass on what someone is saying now, Spanish uses dice que (he/she says that) or dicen que (they say that). Unlike English, you cannot drop que: Andrés dice que va a llegar tarde, never «Andrés dice va a llegar tarde». The verb keeps its tense. If Andrés says «Voy a llegar tarde», you also use the present in your report: va a llegar tarde. What changes is the person: voy (yo) becomes va (él). In a report you do not write quotation marks, a colon or ¿ ? ¡ !: Andrés dice que la reunión es a las cuatro.

titulo.en: Change the person, change the possessive

texto.en: When you pass on a message, think about who is talking and who you are talking about. Andrés says «Mi clase empieza a las ocho» about his own class. You say Dice que su clase empieza a las ocho: mi becomes su. The verbs follow the same logic: necesito becomes necesita, estoy becomes está, vamos becomes van. Su can mean his, her, their or your (ustedes); the context tells you whose it is. Verb patterns you already know work the same way: ir a + infinitive, querer or poder + infinitive and tener que + infinitive stay in the present: «Tengo que salir» becomes dice que tiene que salir.

erroresFrecuentes.incorrecto: Andrés dijo que llegaré a las cuatro.
erroresFrecuentes.correcto: Andrés dijo que llegaría a las cuatro.

explicacion.en: Llegaré is what Andrés said about himself. In your report the verb moves to the él form and to the conditional: llegaría.

titulo.en: What was said, told in the past

texto.en: To report what someone said earlier, use dijo que (he/she said that) or dijeron que, and move the verb one step back in time. When the person was talking about the present, use the imperfect: «Estoy ocupada» becomes dijo que estaba ocupada, «Tengo clase» becomes dijo que tenía clase. The imperfect is a review from N2 and from block 2 of this level: -ar verbs take -aba (necesitaba), -er and -ir verbs take -ía (tenía, quería), and ir a becomes iba a (iba a llamar). Do not use the preterite (necesitó): that would mean a finished event, not what was true when she spoke. In everyday speech people sometimes keep the present if it is still true, but in this lesson use the imperfect.

titulo.en: What was said about the future

texto.en: When the person was talking about the future, use the conditional, which you already know from block 5: «Llegaré a las cuatro» becomes dijo que llegaría a las cuatro; «Pagaré hoy» becomes dijo que pagaría hoy; «Vendré mañana» becomes dijo que vendría mañana (vendr- is irregular). In English the same idea is “would”: he said he would arrive. Pronouns and possessives change exactly as in the last lesson: «mi carro» becomes su carro, «me comunicaré» becomes se comunicaría. So you decide three things: who is speaking now (person), when it was said (past) and whether it was present or future (imperfect or conditional).

explicacion.en: To say where something is located, Spanish uses estar, also inside an indirect question: dónde está.

titulo.en: Passing on a question

texto.en: To pass on a question you do not use ¿ ?. If it is a yes/no question («¿Tienes el número?»), use si: Me preguntó si tengo el número. Careful: si without an accent means “if / whether”; sí with an accent means “yes”. If the question has a question word (dónde, cuándo, cuál, qué, quién, cómo), keep the same word with its accent: «¿Dónde vives?» becomes quiere saber dónde vives. The verb that introduces the question can be preguntar (to ask a question; pedir is to ask for something), querer saber (to want to know), no sé (I do not know) or me pregunto (I wonder).

titulo.en: Word order and tense

texto.en: In Spanish the order of the words does not change when a question becomes indirect: ¿Dónde está el router? becomes no sé dónde está el router. English changes the order (“where is the router” becomes “where the router is”) and Spanish does not. Remember that location uses estar, not ser: dónde está. Also, there is no “do” in Spanish: «¿Dónde trabajas?» is me pregunta dónde trabajo. With a present introducer (me pregunta, quiere saber) the verb stays in the present. After a past introducer (me preguntó) it moves back as you saw in the last lesson: es becomes era, tienes becomes tenía (me preguntó cuál era, me preguntó si tenía). Preterites such as reiniciaron stay in the past: me preguntó si ya reiniciamos el router.

titulo.en: From a question to a reported question

texto.en: Yes/no questions take si. Questions with a question word keep that word, with its accent and without ¿ ?. Tap each sentence to hear it.

titulo.en: Passing on a request or an order

texto.en: To pass on an order or a request, use pedir (or decir) + que + the present subjunctive: Andrés me pide que prepare la lista. The direct order «Prepara la lista» becomes a clause with que and a subjunctive verb. Pedir changes e to i (pido, pides, pide, piden; pedimos does not change). The subjunctive verbs are the ones you reviewed in block 1: prepare, llame, venga, lleguemos. Irregular ones: sea (ser; the tú command is sé), traiga (traer). Do not copy the command form: «Ven mañana» is me pide que venga mañana, never me pide que ven.

titulo.en: Who is asked, and decir that gives orders

texto.en: The pronoun before pide says who must act: me (I), te (you, tú), le (he, she, usted), nos (we), les (they, ustedes). The subjunctive verb agrees with that person: nos pide que lleguemos. Pronouns also change with the speaker: Sofía says «Préstame el proyector» (me = Sofía), but you report Sofía me pide que le preste el proyector (le = Sofía). Decir works like pedir when it gives an order: Andrés me dice que venga means “Andrés tells me to come”, while Andrés dice que viene (last lessons) only passes on information: “Andrés says he is coming”. Compare: the indicative reports facts, the subjunctive reports what someone wants another person to do.

titulo.en: Choosing the right verb

texto.en: Decir (dijo que) works for everything, but Spanish has more precise verbs. Avisar que is to let someone know in advance: schedule changes, warnings, visits (me avisó que vendría un técnico). Explicar que, cómo or por qué gives reasons or says how something works (me explicó que el problema era el cable). Comentar que is to mention something in passing (me comentó que la visita no tendría costo). Contar que is to tell or relate, often news or a story (nos contó que estaba cansada). The pronoun says who is told: me, te, le, nos, les. Notificar, informar, detallar, mencionar and precisar are more formal verbs you read in official messages; responder is simply to answer.

titulo.en: Same pattern as dijo que

texto.en: These verbs follow what you learned in the last lessons. After a verb in the past, use the imperfect for what was true when it was said (el problema era el cable) and the conditional for what was going to happen (vendría un técnico). The pronouns and possessives change with the speaker, and a question word can follow explicar: me explicó cómo funciona, me explicó por qué falla. A general fact that is always true can stay in the present: me explicó cómo funciona el router. Do not drop que before a statement: me avisó que vendría, never «me avisó vendría». Watch contar: it also means to count, and in the present it changes o to ue (cuenta), but not in the preterite (contó).

titulo.en: Four verbs, four shades of meaning

texto.en: All four go with que and follow the pattern of dijo que. Tap each sentence to hear it.

dialogo.texto: Me avisó que un técnico vendría el jueves de la próxima semana.

traduccion.en: She let me know that a technician would come on Thursday of next week.

dialogo.texto: ¿Y cuál es el problema?

traduccion.en: And what is the problem?

dialogo.texto: Me explicó que el problema era el cable que llega al router.

traduccion.en: She explained to me that the problem was the cable that goes to the router.

dialogo.texto: ¿Tiene costo la visita?

traduccion.en: Does the visit have a cost?

dialogo.texto: Me comentó que la visita no tendría costo.

traduccion.en: She mentioned to me that the visit would not have a cost.

dialogo.texto: ¡Qué bien! ¿Y qué más te dijo?

traduccion.en: Great! And what else did she tell you?

dialogo.texto: Me contó que otras escuelas del barrio tenían el mismo problema.

traduccion.en: She told me that other schools in the neighborhood had the same problem.

dialogo.texto: Entonces otras escuelas también tienen el problema. ¿Y qué dijo del router?

traduccion.en: So other schools have the problem too. And what did she say about the router?

dialogo.texto: Me explicó cómo funciona el router y me comentó que el cable era importante.

traduccion.en: She explained to me how the router works and mentioned to me that the cable was important.

dialogo.texto: ¿Tienes algo por correo?

traduccion.en: Do you have anything by email?

dialogo.texto: Sí. El soporte me notificó la visita en un comunicado. En su contestación detalló el problema y precisó la fecha.

traduccion.en: Yes. The support team notified me of the visit in an announcement. In its reply it detailed the problem and specified the date.

dialogo.texto: Muy bien. Gracias por todo, Emma. Te pido que confirmes la hora de la visita.

traduccion.en: Very good. Thanks for everything, Emma. I ask you to confirm the time of the visit.

dialogo.texto: Claro, Andrés. Voy a llamar a la operadora hoy.

traduccion.en: Of course, Andrés. I am going to call the operator today.

dialogo.texto: Perfecto. Yo voy a anotar la fecha en la agenda.

traduccion.en: Perfect. I am going to write down the date in the planner.

consigna.en: According to the dialogue, what did the operator explain was the problem?

feedback.en: Emma says: Me explicó que el problema era el cable que llega al router.

consigna.en: According to the dialogue, what did the operator say about the technician's visit?

feedback.en: Emma says: Me comentó que la visita no tendría costo.

consigna.en: Choose the verb that fits: “The operator ___ me that the technician would come on Thursday.” (let me know in advance)

feedback.en: Avisar is to let someone know in advance: me avisó que vendría el técnico.

consigna.en: Complete with the preterite of explicar: “He explained to me what the problem was.”

feedback.en: The preterite of explicar (él) is explicó: me explicó cuál era el problema.

items.texto: Me ___ cuál era el problema.
items.respuesta: explicó

consigna.en: Put in order: “She let me know that the technician would come.”

feedback.en: Me avisó que vendría el técnico: the technician had not come yet, so vendría is the conditional.

items.respuesta: Me avisó que vendría el técnico
aceptadas: Me avisó que el técnico vendría

consigna.en: Listen. What did he explain?

feedback.en: Nos explicó que el problema era el cable: the problem was the cable.

items.audio: Nos explicó que el problema era el cable.

que el problema era el router

consigna.en: Writing task (at least 14 words, not scored): tell Andrés two things the operator told you, with avisar, explicar, comentar or contar. Compare with the model.

feedback.en: Model: La operadora me avisó que un técnico vendría el jueves. También me explicó que el problema era el cable.
